{{nihongo|'''Obori Shrine'''|小祝神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kōzuke Province]].

'''Obori Shrine''' (おぼりじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Ishihara-chō, {{ill|Takasaki|Q336438|qid=Q336438}}, {{ill|Gunma Prefecture|Q129499|qid=Q129499}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, the {{ill|Kōzuke Province|Q1054838|qid=Q1054838}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Nanamiya}}, and its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}. Its {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=shrine crest}} is “Mitsudomoe”{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}.

Its old name in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} was “Obori Daimyōjin.”

=== Enshrined deity ===
The enshrined deity is the following one<ref>[http://www.raijin.com/obori/html/yurai/htm Origin of Obori Shrine] (official site).</ref>.
* {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto}}

In the '{{ill|Shintōshū|Q2616931|qid=Q2616931}},' the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=honji-butsu}} is {{ill|Manjushri|Q471696|qid=Q471696}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}. However, early-modern origin records mention {{ill|Bhaisajyaguru|bg|Буда лечител|bn|ভৈষজ্যগুরু|bo|སྨན་བླ།|ca|Bhaishajyaguru|cs|Bhaišadžjaguru|de|Bhaisajyaguru|es|Bhaisajyaguru|fr|Bhaishajyaguru|hi|भैषज्यगुरु|hu|Bhaisadzsjaguru|id|Bhaiṣajyaguru|it|Bhaiṣajyaguru|ja|薬師如来|ko|약사여래|nl|Bhaisajyaguru|pl|Bhajszadźja|ro|Bhaisajyaguru|ru|Будда Медицины|si|භෛශජ්‍යගුරු බුදුන් වහන්සේ|sv|Bhaisajyaguru|ta|பைசையகுரு|te|భైషజ్యగురు బుద్ధుడు|th|พระไภษัชยคุรุ|tyv|Очуду|uk|Бгайсадж'я-гуру|ur|بھئشجیاگرو وئڈوریاپربھاراجہ|vi|Phật Dược Sư|wuu|药师佛|zh|藥師佛|qid=Q854773|lt=Yakushi}}, and a Yakushi hall also existed behind the shrine{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}. A document of {{ill|1717|Q6895|qid=Q6895}} ({{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}} 2) describes the {{ill|Shintai|Q327532|qid=Q327532}} as stone{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}. Also, the 'Shikinaisha Survey Report' says there are 21 additional deities besides Sukunahikona-no-Mikoto{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}.

=== History ===
=== Founding ===
Founding is unknown. Nearby is Mishimazuka Kofun (a late 4th to early 5th century {{ill|Round Kofun|Q11394747|qid=Q11394747}}), and early Jōmon pottery fragments were excavated from the precincts, suggesting the shrine has stood here since ancient times{{Sfn|小祝神社（神々）|1984年}}.

The clan that originally worshipped this shrine is unknown. The 'Kōzuke no Kuni Jinmyōchō' records “Sokusai-ji Obori Myōjin” in western Gunma district, and this “Sokusai-ji” is identified with {{ill|Myokenji Temple (Hikimacho, Takasaki City)|Q11447022|qid=Q11447022}} near the Kōzuke provincial office. From this, the clan serving Obori deity is thought to have become provincial officials, and “Sokusai-ji Obori Myōjin” is inferred to have been invited from this shrine as ujigami to Sokusai-ji built near the provincial office{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}{{Sfn|小祝神社（平）|1987年}}{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}.

=== Overview history ===
Founding is unknown. In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=official national histories}}, there is a record that the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of “Obori-no-Kami” was promoted in {{ill|880|Q23618|qid=Q23618}} ({{ill|Gangyō|Q747451|qid=Q747451}} 4) from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper, rank-12 merit{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}.

In the '{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}' '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' compiled in Enchō 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), it appears in {{ill|Kataoka District, Gunma|Q11569784|qid=Q11569784}} of {{ill|Kōzuke Province|Q1054838|qid=Q1054838}} as “Obori Shrine,” and is listed as {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}. The same register gives the contemporary reading as “Ohafuri”{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}.

In the 'Kōzuke no Kuni Jinmyōchō,' the Sōja text shows “Senior First Rank Obori Daimyōjin” as 7th among ten guardian shrines, while the Ichinomiya text shows it 4th, and the 'Gunsho Ruijū' text 6th, each as “Junior First Rank Obori Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|小祝神社（神々）|1984年}}. As related deity name, as noted above, “Junior Third Rank Sokusai-ji Obori Myōjin” appears in west Gunma district{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}.

In the '{{ill|Shintōshū|Q2616931|qid=Q2616931}}' compiled in the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|Q264012|qid=Q264012}}, “Jōzuke no Kuni kyūkasho daimyōjin” states “Nanamiya is Sawa-miya, called Koshi (likely mistaken for Obori), honji is Monju,” and the shrine is considered Kōzuke’s {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Nanamiya}}{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}}.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was granted Senior First Rank by {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sōgen senji}} in {{ill|1716|Q6892|qid=Q6892}} ({{ill|Shōtoku (era)|Q1193848|qid=Q1193848|lt=Shōtoku}} 6){{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}. In {{ill|1717|Q6895|qid=Q6895}} (Kyōhō 2), the current main sanctuary was built{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}. The {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}} {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}} was Sekishō-ji{{Sfn|中世諸国一宮制|2000年|p=282}} (still adjacent today).

In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), it was ranked {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gōsha}} under the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=modern shrine rank system}}, and in {{ill|1909|ab|1909|af|1909|als|1909|am|1909 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1909|ar|1909|ary|1909|arz|1909|ast|1909|av|1909|avk|1909|az|1909|azb|۱۹۰۹ (میلادی)|ba|1909 йыл|ban|1909|bar|1909|bat_smg|1909|bcl|1909|be|1909|be_x_old|1909|bg|1909|bh|1909|bn|১৯০৯|bpy|মারি ১৯০৯|br|1909|bs|1909.|ca|1909|cdo|1909 nièng|ce|1909 шо|ceb|1909|ckb|١٩٠٩|co|1909|crh|1909|cs|1909|csb|1909|cv|1909|cy|1909|da|1909|de|1909|diq|1909|dsb|1909|el|1909|eml|1909|eo|1909|es|1909|et|1909|eu|1909|ext|1909|fa|۱۹۰۹|fi|1909|fiu_vro|1909|fo|1909|fr|1909|frp|1909|frr|1909|fur|1909|fy|1909|ga|1909|gag|1909|gan|1909年|gcr|1909|gd|1909|gl|1909|gn|1909|gv|1909|hak|1909-ngièn|he|1909|hi|१९०९|hif|1909|hr|1909.|hsb|1909|ht|1909 (almanak gregoryen)|hu|1909|hy|1909|hyw|1909 թուական|ia|1909|id|1909|ig|1909|ilo|1909|inh|1909 шу|io|1909|is|1909|it|1909|ja|1909年|jv|1909|ka|1909|kaa|1909|kbp|1909|kk|1909 жыл|kn|೧೯೦೯|ko|1909년|krc|1909 джыл|ksh|Joohr 1909|ku|1909|kv|1909-ӧд во|kw|1909|la|1909|lb|1909|lez|1909 йис|li|1909|lij|1909|lmo|1909|lt|1909 m.|lv|1909. gads|mai|१९०९|map_bms|1909|mdf|1909|mg|1909|mhr|1909|mi|1909|min|1909|mk|1909|ml|1909|mn|1909 он|mr|इ.स. १९०९|mrj|1909 и|ms|1909|my|၁၉၀၉|myv|1909 ие|mzn|۱۹۰۹|nah|1909|nap|1909|nds|1909|new|ई सं १९०९|nl|1909|nn|1909|no|1909|nov|1909|nrm|1909|nso|1909|oc|1909|olo|1909|or|୧୯୦୯|os|1909-æм аз|pa|1909|pam|1909|pap|1909|pl|1909|pms|1909|pnb|1909|pt|1909|qu|1909|ro|1909|roa_tara|1909|ru|1909 год|rue|1909|sah|1909|sc|1909|scn|1909|sco|1909|sd|1909ع|se|1909|sh|1909.|shn|1909|simple|1909|sk|1909|sl|1909|smn|1909|sq|1909|sr|1909|srn|1909|stq|1909|su|1909|sv|1909|sw|1909|szl|1909|ta|1909|te|1909|tg|Соли 1909|th|พ.ศ. 2452|tk|1909|tl|1909|tly|1909|tpi|1909|tr|1909|tt|1909 ел|ty|1909|udm|1909 ар|ug|1909 - يىلى|uk|1909|ur|1909ء|uz|1909|vec|1909|vi|1909|vls|1909|vo|1909|wa|1909|war|1909|wuu|1909年|xmf|1909|yi|1909|za|1909 nienz|zea|1909|zh|1909年|zh_classical|一九〇九年|zh_min_nan|1909 nî|zh_yue|1909年|qid=Q2057}} (Meiji 42), it was designated as a shrine receiving offerings of sacred food and cloth{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Obori-jinja honden.JPG|thumb|250px|right|Main sanctuary (Takasaki City-designated Important Cultural Property)]]
The current main shrine buildings consist of main sanctuary, heiden, and worship hall in an integrated form. However, the heiden and worship hall were built later than the main sanctuary. Documents and dedication plaques indicate reconstruction was planned in Shōtoku 3 ({{ill|1713|Q6873|qid=Q6873}}) and ridge-raising completed in Kyōhō 2 ({{ill|1717|Q6895|qid=Q6895}}). The style is three-bay {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}, with three bays on the sides and a three-bay front kōhai. The roof is now copper plate, though originally likely {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}} or kokera-buki. Interior is divided into outer chamber (front two bays) and inner sanctuary (rear one bay), with a {{ill|Zushi|Q19993032|qid=Q19993032}} installed in the inner sanctuary. This main sanctuary is the oldest shrine main sanctuary in Takasaki, and its rear inset carved panel (oldest example in Gunma) serves as a chronological benchmark for similar works; with munafuda, dedication plaque, and donor inscription it is designated Takasaki City Important Cultural Property<ref>Precinct explanation board.</ref><ref name="本殿"/>{{Sfn|小祝神社（式内社）|1986年}}.
